stops.note: from a language of inland south-eastern Australia, though which one is uncertain; peoples such as the Yandruwandha of Cooper Creek ground its spore cases into flour after soaking and washing them
Burke and Wills lived on nardoo at Cooper Creek in 1861 but prepared it without the Aboriginal washing method, likely leaving them short of thiamine; John King survived with Yandruwandha help

current_meaning: an Australian clover-like fern whose spore cases were ground for flour
